title: Jaisalmer: The Golden City of Rajasthan
content:
Jaisalmer 

Jaisalmer, popularly known as the Golden City, is one of the most beautiful destinations in Rajasthan. The city gets its name from the golden sandstone used in its architecture, which glows magically under the sunlight. Surrounded by the vast Thar Desert, Jaisalmer is a perfect blend of royal heritage, desert adventures, and cultural charm.

The main attraction of Jaisalmer is the Jaisalmer Fort (Sonar Quila), a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the few living forts in the world where people still reside inside. The fort is home to temples, shops, and havelis that reflect centuries of history. Another highlight is the Patwon Ki Haveli, known for its intricate carvings and detailed artwork, while Salim Singh Ki Haveli and Nathmal Ki Haveli showcase the rich craftsmanship of Rajasthan.

For nature and adventure lovers, the Sam Sand Dunes offer an unforgettable desert experience. Visitors can enjoy camel rides, jeep safaris, and cultural performances while staying in luxury desert camps under the starry sky. The Gadisar Lake is another peaceful spot, perfect for photography and enjoying serene views. Shopping in Jaisalmer is also a delightful experience, with colorful handicrafts, textiles, and puppets available in local markets.

The best time to visit Jaisalmer is from October to March, when the weather is cool and pleasant. A 2 to 3-day trip is enough to explore the fort, havelis, and desert safari. If you visit in February, you can also witness the famous Jaisalmer Desert Festival, which showcases Rajasthani music, dance, camel races, and vibrant cultural traditions.

Jaisalmer is not just a city but an experience that brings history, culture, and desert beauty together in one place. From royal forts to golden sands, this destination truly deserves a spot on every traveler’s Rajasthan itinerary.

Top Attractions in Jaisalmer

1. Jaisalmer Fort (Sonar Quila)

 

Jaisalmer Fort, also known as Sonar Qila (Golden Fort), is a magnificent sandstone fort located in the heart of the Thar Desert in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. Built in 1156 AD by Rawal Jaisal, it is one of the largest and oldest living forts in the world, still inhabited by local residents. The fort is made of golden-yellow sandstone, giving it a glowing appearance, especially at sunrise and sunset.

Perched on Trikuta Hill, the fort features massive walls, 99 bastions, palaces, Hindu and Jain temples, and narrow lanes filled with shops, cafés, and homes. Major attractions include the Raj Mahal, Jain Temples, and Laxminath Temple. Once a key trade hub on the Silk Route, the fort remains a vibrant cultural center.

Entry Fee (for museum section): Indians: ₹50–₹100, Foreigners: ₹200–₹500, Camera fee extra

Timings: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM (daily)

 

2. Sam Sand Dunes


Perfect for desert safaris, camel rides, jeep adventures, and cultural performances under the starlit sky.Sam Sand Dunes are one of the most popular tourist attractions near Jaisalmer, located about 40 km west of the city in the heart of the Thar Desert, Rajasthan. These vast, rolling sand dunes offer an authentic desert experience with golden landscapes, especially stunning at sunrise and sunset.

Visitors can enjoy a range of activities, including camel rides, jeep safaris, quad biking, and dune bashing. The area is also known for its desert camps, where you can stay overnight in luxury tents and enjoy Rajasthani folk music, dance performances, and local cuisine under the stars. The best time to visit is between October and March, when the weather is cooler and desert festivals are held.3. Patwon Ki Haveli
A group of five havelis with intricate carvings, reflecting the grandeur of Rajasthan’s architecture.

 

3. Gadisar Lake


 

Gadisar Lake is a beautiful man-made lake located on the outskirts of Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. It was built in the 14th century by Maharawal Gadsi Singh as a water conservation reservoir for the arid region and served as the city's main water source for centuries.

Surrounded by temples, shrines, and ghats, the lake offers a peaceful setting and scenic views, especially during sunrise and sunset. One of its most iconic features is the Tilon ki Pol, an intricately carved stone archway at the entrance. Visitors can enjoy boating on the lake, spot migratory birds (especially in winter), and explore the surrounding heritage structures.

Open all day with free entry (boating charges extra), Gadisar Lake is a serene retreat from the desert heat and a perfect spot for photography, relaxation, and light sightseeing in Jaisalmer.
 

4. Salim Singh Ki Haveli 


Salim Singh Ki Haveli is a striking 18th-century mansion located in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, known for its distinctive architecture and historical significance. It was built around 1815 AD by Salim Singh, the powerful Prime Minister (Diwan) of Jaisalmer, during the reign of Maharawal Gaj Singh.

The haveli is famous for its arched roof, designed to resemble a peacock, and its narrow, tall structure that rises seven stories high. The most impressive feature is the upper floor with 38 intricately carved balconies, each with a unique design, showcasing excellent Rajput architecture and stone craftsmanship.

Unlike other havelis in Jaisalmer, Salim Singh Ki Haveli has a distinctive and dramatic appearance, with curved brackets, blue cupolas, and delicate jharokhas (overhanging windows). It was originally intended to be even taller than the royal palace but was stopped by the king.

Open to visitors daily from 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

5. Nathmal Ki Haveli


Nathmal Ki Haveli is a beautiful 19th-century mansion located in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, known for its intricate carvings, unique architecture, and fascinating story behind its construction. It was built by two architect brothers, Lalu and Hathi, who worked simultaneously but independently on the two sides of the haveli, resulting in a perfectly symmetrical but slightly different design on each half.

Commissioned as the residence of Diwan Mohata Nathmal, the then Prime Minister of Jaisalmer, the haveli is a fine example of Rajput-Islamic architecture blended with some surprising modern elements—like carvings of cars, fans, and flowers, which were added based on images and stories brought by travelers from abroad.

Made of golden-yellow sandstone, the haveli features delicately carved jharokhas (balconies), elephant sculptures at the entrance, and richly decorated interiors with paintings and mirror work. It is still partially inhabited, but visitors can explore parts of the building.

Open from 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM

 

6. Kuldhara Village

 

Kuldhara Village is a famous abandoned village located about 18 km from Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. Once a thriving settlement of Paliwal Brahmins, it was mysteriously deserted overnight in the early 19th century, and since then, it has remained uninhabited, earning a reputation as a haunted village.

According to legend, the village was abandoned due to the oppressive demands of Salim Singh, the then-powerful minister of Jaisalmer, who wanted to forcibly marry a local girl. To protect their honor and unity, the villagers of Kuldhara - and 83 nearby villages - reportedly vanished overnight, leaving no trace of their whereabouts. It is said they cursed the land so that no one could settle there again.

Today, Kuldhara is a protected heritage site maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India. Visitors can walk among the ruins of sandstone houses, narrow lanes, and the village temple, all set against the stark beauty of the Thar Desert. Despite its eerie reputation, Kuldhara attracts many tourists, especially those interested in history, mystery, and photography.

The site is open daily from 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM, and there is a small entry fee.

7. Tanot Mata Temple - The Divine Guardian of Jaisalmer

 

Tanot Mata Temple, located near the India-Pakistan border in Jaisalmer district, is one of the most revered temples in Rajasthan. Dedicated to Goddess Tanot (an incarnation of Hinglaj Mata), the temple is not only a place of deep faith but also a site of historical and military importance.

During the Indo-Pak wars of 1965 and 1971, it is believed that several bombs dropped near the temple failed to explode, protecting both the temple and the soldiers. This miracle turned Tanot Mata Temple into a symbol of divine protection and strength, and since then, it has been maintained with the support of the Border Security Force (BSF).

Pilgrims and tourists visit the temple not only to seek blessings but also to witness the museum maintained by BSF, which displays weapons and stories of bravery from the wars. Surrounded by desert landscapes, the temple also offers a glimpse into the unique culture and faith of the region.

  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Timings: 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March (winter months are ideal for desert travel)
  • Location: Around 120 km from Jaisalmer city, en route to Longewala

 

8. Kothari’s Patwaon Ki Haveli - The Pride of Jaisalmer’s Golden Architecture

 

Kothari’s Patwaon Ki Haveli, located in the heart of Jaisalmer, is one of the most magnificent and famous havelis (mansions) in Rajasthan. Built in the early 19th century by Guman Chand Patwa, a wealthy trader, it is actually a cluster of five havelis, each adorned with stunning carvings, intricate jharokhas (balconies), and golden-yellow sandstone facades.

This haveli is an architectural masterpiece that reflects the opulence of Jaisalmer’s merchant class during its golden era. The interiors are equally mesmerizing, featuring beautiful wall paintings, mirror work, arches, and artifacts that showcase the region’s rich cultural heritage. Today, parts of the haveli have been converted into a museum, where visitors can explore the lifestyle of the Patwa family and admire priceless antiques.

Often called the “mansion of brocade merchants”, Patwaon Ki Haveli is a must-visit for history lovers, art enthusiasts, and photographers who wish to experience the grandeur of Jaisalmer’s past.

  • Entry Fee: ₹20 (Indians), ₹100 (Foreigners) approx.
  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March for comfortable sightseeing

9. Longewala War Memorial - A Tribute to India’s Bravery

 

The Longewala War Memorial, located about 120 km from Jaisalmer, is a historic site that commemorates the heroic battle fought during the Indo-Pak War of 1971. At this very battlefield, a small group of 120 Indian soldiers of the Punjab Regiment, with the support of the Indian Air Force, bravely defended against a much larger Pakistani force, turning the battle into one of India’s most remarkable victories.

Maintained by the Indian Army, the memorial showcases tanks, jeeps, bunkers, and other war relics used during the battle. Visitors can also watch a short documentary at the memorial’s museum, which narrates the story of courage, strategy, and sacrifice that took place at Longewala.

Surrounded by the stark yet beautiful Thar Desert, the Longewala War Memorial is not just a tourist attraction but also a place that fills every Indian with pride and respect for the armed forces.

  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Timings: 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March (to avoid the desert heat)
  • Location: Around 120 km from Jaisalmer city, on the way to Tanot Mata Temple

 

10. Bada Bagh - The Royal Cenotaphs of Jaisalmer

 

Bada Bagh, which means “Big Garden”, is one of the most enchanting heritage sites in Jaisalmer. Located about 6 km north of the city, it is famous for its collection of cenotaphs (chhatris) built in memory of the royal family of Jaisalmer. The site was commissioned by Maharaja Jai Singh in the 16th century and later continued by his descendants.

The cenotaphs are carved from golden-yellow sandstone, beautifully decorated with intricate designs, and set against the backdrop of the desert landscape. Each chhatri is dedicated to a king or queen of Jaisalmer, and together they create a breathtaking view, especially during sunrise and sunset, when the golden structures glow with the desert light.

Bada Bagh is not just a historical site but also a place of tranquility, making it a favorite spot for photographers, history lovers, and peace seekers.

  • Entry Fee: ₹100 (Indians), ₹200 (Foreigners) approx.
  • Timings: 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March, ideally during sunrise or sunset for the best views

 

11. Jaisalmer War Museum - A Tribute to Bravery 🇮🇳

 

The Jaisalmer War Museum, also known as JWM, is a proud tribute to the Indian Army’s bravery and sacrifice. Located on the Jaisalmer-Jodhpur Highway, it was set up by the Indian Army’s Desert Corps to honor the heroes of the 1965 and 1971 Indo-Pak wars.

The museum showcases tanks, military vehicles, weapons, and war memorabilia, giving visitors a glimpse into the valor and dedication of Indian soldiers. The highlight is the Hunter Aircraft, which played a key role in the Longewala Battle during the 1971 war.

There are two main halls inside:

Laungewala Hall - narrates the story of the Battle of Longewala, a historic victory for India.

Indian Army Hall - displays the Army’s contributions in various wars and humanitarian missions.

The Audio-Visual Room screens war movies and documentaries, making the experience more engaging and emotional.

  • Best Time to Visit: October to March
  • Location: Jaisalmer-Jodhpur Highway, about 10 km from Jaisalmer City
  • Tip: Don’t miss the evening Light & Sound Show, which beautifully tells the story of Indian soldiers’ courage.

 

12. Jain Temples - Jaisalmer’s Architectural Gems 

 

The Jain Temples in Jaisalmer are a group of beautifully carved shrines located inside the Jaisalmer Fort. Built between the 12th and 16th centuries, these temples are dedicated to different Tirthankaras (spiritual teachers of Jainism).

The temples are made of yellow sandstone, with intricate carvings, detailed sculptures, and fine artwork that showcase the rich craftsmanship of Rajasthan. The interiors are equally stunning, with pillars, domes, and walls decorated with delicate carvings of gods, celestial beings, and animals.

Some of the main temples include:

Chandraprabhu Temple - dedicated to the 8th Tirthankara.

Rishabhdev Temple - devoted to the first Tirthankara.

Parshvanath Temple - the largest of all, with magnificent architecture.

Apart from being religious sites, these temples are also treasures of art, history, and architecture. Visitors must remove their shoes before entering and maintain silence to respect the sacred environment.

  • Best Time to Visit: October to March
  • Location: Inside Jaisalmer Fort
  • Tip: Morning visits are best, as the sunlight enhances the golden glow of the sandstone carvings.

 

13. Basant Art Emporium - A Shopper’s Delight in Jaisalmer

 

Basant Art Emporium in Jaisalmer is a popular destination for travelers who want to take home a piece of Rajasthan’s artistic heritage. Known for its handcrafted textiles, embroidery, paintings, and traditional Rajasthani artwork, the emporium is a treasure house of creativity.

Here, you can find:

Hand-embroidered fabrics with mirror work and patchwork.

Rajasthani paintings including miniature art.

Home décor items like wall hangings, carpets, and cushions.

Handicrafts made of wood, metal, and stone.

The emporium is especially famous for its quality and authenticity, making it a favorite among tourists looking for souvenirs. The friendly staff often explains the stories behind the artwork, giving visitors a cultural experience along with shopping.

  • Best For: Souvenirs, traditional Rajasthani art, textiles
  • Location: Near Fort area, Jaisalmer
  • Tip: Bargaining is limited here as it is known for genuine pricing, but always check quality before buying.

 

14. Desert Culture Centre & Museum - Preserving Jaisalmer’s Heritage

 

The Desert Culture Centre & Museum in Jaisalmer is a must-visit for anyone interested in the history, traditions, and lifestyle of Rajasthan’s desert communities. Founded by Mr. N. K. Sharma, the museum showcases a wide collection of folk art, textiles, manuscripts, coins, fossils, and traditional instruments.

A highlight of the museum is the puppet show, which brings Rajasthani folklore to life and offers entertainment along with cultural education. Visitors can also explore displays of ancient weapons, turbans, and unique artifacts that reflect the desert way of life.

  • Best For: History lovers, cultural explorers, and families
  • Location: Opposite Lake Gadisar, Jaisalmer
  • Timings: 10:00 AM - 6:00 PM (Puppet show in the evening)
  • Entry Fee: Around ₹20 - ₹50 (extra for puppet show)

 

15. Raj Camel Safari - An Authentic Desert Experience in Jaisalmer

 

The Raj Camel Safari is one of the most popular ways to experience the golden sands of the Thar Desert in Jaisalmer. This safari offers travelers a chance to ride on camels, explore sand dunes, and witness the breathtaking sunset over the desert horizon.

Along with camel rides, visitors can enjoy cultural performances, folk music, traditional dance, and local Rajasthani cuisine under the starlit sky. Some packages also include overnight stays in desert camps, providing a magical experience of sleeping under the open desert sky.

  • Best For: Adventure seekers, couples, and families
  • Location: Starting points vary (commonly from Jaisalmer city to Sam or Khuri Sand Dunes)
  • Timings: Morning & evening safaris available (best time - sunset)
  • Charges: ₹500 - ₹1,500 (depending on package; overnight stays cost extra)

 

16. Desert Art Gallery - A Hub of Rajasthani Creativity

 

The Desert Art Gallery in Jaisalmer is a charming place that showcases the rich art, handicrafts, and cultural heritage of Rajasthan. It is especially known for its exquisite paintings, miniature artwork, and traditional Rajasthani crafts created by skilled local artisans.

Visitors can explore handmade souvenirs, embroidery, textiles, leather items, and decorative pieces, making it a perfect spot to buy authentic Rajasthani art. The gallery not only promotes local artists but also gives tourists a chance to take home a piece of Jaisalmer’s cultural essence.

  • Location: Near Jaisalmer Fort, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 7:00 PM (all days)
  • Entry Fee: Free (charges apply only for purchases)

 

17. Ramdevra Temple - A Sacred Pilgrimage Near Jaisalmer

 

The Ramdevra Temple, located about 12 km from Pokhran and around 135 km from Jaisalmer, is one of the most revered temples in Rajasthan. Dedicated to Baba Ramdevji, a 14th-century saint who is believed to be an incarnation of Lord Krishna, this temple attracts devotees from all over India.

Every year, thousands of pilgrims visit the temple during the Ramdevra Fair (August–September) to pay homage to Baba Ramdevji. The temple is not only a religious site but also a symbol of faith, unity, and devotion, where people of all communities come together to worship.

  • Location: Ramdevra Village, near Pokhran, Rajasthan
  • Timings: 5:00 AM - 9:00 PM (all days)
  • Entry Fee: Free

 

18. Vyas Chhatri - The Sunset Point of Jaisalmer

 

The Vyas Chhatri is a beautiful sandstone cenotaph dedicated to Sage Vyas, the author of the Mahabharata. Located on the edge of Jaisalmer, it is one of the most serene and picturesque places in the city. The cenotaphs are intricately carved and built in the classic Rajasthani style of architecture, representing the grandeur of Jaisalmer’s royal past.

This spot is especially famous as a sunset point, where the golden rays fall over the desert and sandstone structures, creating a breathtaking view. It is also a quiet place to enjoy photography, history, and peace away from the bustling markets.

  • Location: Near Jaisalmer Fort, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
  • Timings: 8:00 AM - 7:30 PM (all days)
  • Entry Fee: ₹100 (approx.)

 

19. Maharaja’s Palace - The Royal Gem of Jaisalmer Fort

 

The Maharaja’s Palace, located inside the majestic Jaisalmer Fort, is a stunning example of Rajput royalty and grandeur. This palace served as the residence of the rulers of Jaisalmer and showcases intricate carvings, grand courtyards, balconies, and ornate designs that reflect the richness of Rajasthan’s heritage.

Inside the palace, visitors can explore royal chambers, artifacts, and a museum displaying ancient weapons, costumes, and paintings. The palace also offers panoramic views of Jaisalmer city from its top, making it a must-visit attraction for history lovers and photography enthusiasts.

  • Location: Inside Jaisalmer Fort, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
  • Timings: 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM (all days)  
  • Entry Fee: ₹250 (approx.)

 

20. Khaba Fort - The Abandoned Beauty of Jaisalme

 

The Khaba Fort, located around 35 km from Jaisalmer, is a mysterious and historic site that once belonged to the Paliwal Brahmins who lived here about 200 years ago. The fort now stands in ruins but still reflects the royal charm and architectural elegance of Rajasthan.

Surrounded by an abandoned village, Khaba Fort is often called a haunted site due to the sudden desertion of the Paliwal community. It is a fascinating destination for history buffs, photographers, and those curious about Rajasthan’s legends. From the fort, visitors can also enjoy stunning views of the Thar Desert.

  • Location: Khaba Village, 35 km from Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
  • Timings: 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM (all days)
  • Entry Fee: ₹50 (approx.)

 

21. Amar Sagar Lake - A Peaceful Oasis in Jaisalmer 

 

The Amar Sagar Lake, located about 7 km from Jaisalmer, is a serene and picturesque water reservoir built in the 17th century by Maharawal Amar Singh. Surrounded by beautifully carved cenotaphs (chhatris) and an ancient Shiva temple, this lake is a perfect spot for those who love peace, photography, and heritage.

During the monsoon season, the lake gets filled with water, turning it into a scenic retreat amidst the golden desert. The calm surroundings and architectural beauty make it a hidden gem for travelers exploring Jaisalmer.

  • Location: 7 km from Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free

 

22. The Thar Heritage Museum - A Glimpse into Desert Culture 

 

The Thar Heritage Museum, located near Gandhi Chowk in Jaisalmer, is a must-visit for those interested in learning about the rich history, culture, and traditions of Rajasthan’s desert region. Established by folklorist Laxmi Narayan Khatri, this museum beautifully preserves the heritage of the Thar Desert.

Inside, visitors can explore a fascinating collection of ancient manuscripts, coins, fossils, weapons, musical instruments, traditional costumes, and artifacts. The museum also hosts folk performances and puppet shows, offering an engaging cultural experience for tourists.

  • Location: Gandhi Chowk, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: ₹30 - ₹50 (approx.)

 

23. Akal Wood Fossil Park - A Natural Wonder of Prehistoric Times

 

The Akal Wood Fossil Park, located about 17 km from Jaisalmer, is a fascinating site that takes visitors back to the Jurassic era, nearly 180 million years ago. Spread over 21 hectares, the park preserves the remains of fossilized trees and plants, giving a glimpse into the time when the Thar Desert was once a lush forest.

This unique destination is perfect for nature lovers, geologists, and history enthusiasts who wish to explore Rajasthan’s prehistoric secrets. The fossil trunks and preserved remains are rare finds that make the park a true natural wonder of Jaisalmer.

  • Location: Akal Village, 17 km from Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: ₹20 (Indians), ₹100 (Foreigners)

 

24. Mandir Palace - A Royal Heritage Stay in Jaisalmer

 

The Mandir Palace, located in the heart of Jaisalmer city, is a magnificent heritage palace that once served as the residence of the royal family. Known for its intricate stone carvings, ornate balconies, jharokhas, and tall structures, the palace beautifully reflects the architectural brilliance of Rajasthan.

One of the highlights of the palace is its ‘Badal Vilas’ tower, which stands out as the tallest structure in the city. Today, part of Mandir Palace has been converted into a luxury heritage hotel, offering guests a chance to experience royal living with modern comforts. Visitors can also explore its museum section, which showcases royal artifacts and historical collections.

  • Location: Near Gandhi Chowk, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
  • Timings: 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM (for museum visits)
  • Entry Fee: ₹50 – ₹100 (approx., for museum)

 

25. Jaisalmer Desert Festival - A Celebration of Culture and Colors

 

The Jaisalmer Desert Festival is one of the most vibrant and iconic cultural events of Rajasthan, held every year in the month of February amidst the golden sands of the Thar Desert. Organized by the Rajasthan Tourism Department, this three-day festival showcases the rich heritage, music, dance, and traditions of the desert state.

Highlights of the festival include folk music and dance performances, camel races, turban-tying competitions, puppet shows, desert processions, and even a Mr. Desert contest. Visitors also enjoy the colorful bazaars, local handicrafts, and authentic Rajasthani cuisine.

The festival is a visual treat, with the sand dunes near Sam village coming alive with lights, colors, and performances under the starlit desert sky. It is a must-visit event for travelers looking to experience Rajasthan’s culture in its most authentic form.

  • Location: Sam Sand Dunes, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
  • Timing: Held every year in February (3-day festival)
  • Entry Fee: Free (charges apply for certain activities or safaris)

 

26. Jaisalmer Sunset Point - A Magical View of the Golden City


 

The Jaisalmer Sunset Point is one of the most scenic spots to witness the golden hues of the Thar Desert as the sun sets behind the sandstone city. From this viewpoint, travelers can enjoy breathtaking views of Jaisalmer Fort, desert landscapes, and traditional houses glowing under the evening sky.

It is a favorite place for photographers, couples, and nature lovers, offering a peaceful atmosphere away from the busy city streets. The view of the sun slowly dipping into the horizon, painting the desert in shades of orange and gold, makes it an unforgettable experience.

  • Location: Near Vyas Chhatri, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
  • Timings: Best visited during sunset (around 5:30 PM - 7:00 PM, depending on season)
  • Entry Fee: Free

 

27. Amar Sagar Jain Temple - A Spiritual Gem of Jaisalmer

 

The Amar Sagar Jain Temple, located near Amar Sagar Lake about 7 km from Jaisalmer, is a stunning piece of Jain architecture and devotion. Built in the 17th century by the royal family of Jaisalmer, the temple is dedicated to Lord Parshvanath, the 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism.

The temple is famous for its intricate stone carvings, delicate sculptures, and beautifully designed pillars, which reflect the craftsmanship of Jaisalmer’s artisans. Surrounded by a tranquil environment, it is not only a spiritual site but also a serene retreat for visitors.

  • Location: Near Amar Sagar Lake, 7 km from Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
  • Timings: 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free

28. Sonee Art Gallery - A Creative Hub in Jaisalmer

 

The Sonee Art Gallery in Jaisalmer is a wonderful place for art enthusiasts to explore the vibrant culture and artistic traditions of Rajasthan. The gallery showcases a wide range of miniature paintings, traditional Rajasthani artwork, portraits, and handcrafted pieces, all made by skilled local artists.

Visitors can not only admire the detailed artistry but also purchase unique souvenirs, making it a perfect stop for those who want to take home a piece of Jaisalmer’s heritage. The gallery is well-known for its warm hospitality and authentic collection, making it a must-visit for travelers.

Location: Near Jaisalmer Fort, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
Timings: 9:00 AM - 7:00 PM
Entry Fee: Free (charges apply only for purchases)
excerpt: Jaisalmer, the Golden City of Rajasthan, is a desert gem famous for its golden fort, sand dunes, havelis, and vibrant culture. From camel safaris to desert camping, Jaisalmer offers a royal and adventurous experience in the heart of the Thar Desert.
